questions.question: Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. I like my new office.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

I like my new office.

options.text: I am liking my new office.
options.html: I am liking my new office.

options.text: My new office was liked by me.
options.html: My new office was liked by me.

options.text: My new office has been liked by me.
options.html: My new office has been liked by me.

options.text: My new office is liked by me.
options.html: My new office is liked by me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'My new office is liked by me'.

Key Points  

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the active voice and 'I' is the subject and 'my new office' is the object.
  • When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'I' of the active voice becomes the object 'me', the object 'my new office' becomes the subject.
  • The passive format "'is + V3 (liked)" should be used.
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the present simple tense.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Additional Information

  • Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:
     
    TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION
    Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him
    Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him
    Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him
    Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual
    Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him
    Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him
    Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him
    Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him
    Future Continuous He will be playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him
    Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual

options.html: Chocolate is being liked by Ravish.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Key Points

  • In the original sentence, "likes" is in the simple present tense, so we need to maintain the same tense in the passive voice.
  • When changing a sentence from active to passive voice, the object of the active sentence (here "chocolate") becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
  • The verb 'like' changes to 'is liked' to match the tense and the passive structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: 'Chocolate is liked by Ravish.'

Additional Information

  • Here's why the other options are incorrect:
    • "Chocolate was liked by Ravish." - This uses the past tense ("was liked"), which changes the original tense of the sentence.
    • "Chocolate were liked by Ravish." - This is grammatically incorrect because "were liked" should be used with plural subjects, and "chocolate" is singular.
    • "Chocolate is being liked by Ravish." - The phrase "is being liked" suggests an ongoing action, which changes the tense and the meaning of the original sentence. "Like" is also a stative verb, which doesn't usually use continuous (progressive) tenses.

The correct answer is Option (4) "Suman's pocket has been picked."  Key Points

  • The sentence is in passive voice, which means the subject of given sentence will not do any work itself.
  • Instead, the focus is on the object (Suman's pocket) and the action that was done to it (picked).
  • The verb "picked" is in the past participle form, which is used in passive voice constructions.
  • It is formed by adding "-ed" to regular verbs or using the third form of irregular verbs.
  •  The auxiliary verb "has been" is used to form the present perfect passive tense. This indicates that the action happened at an unspecified time before now and has ongoing effects.
  •  In active voice, the sentence would be "Someone has picked Suman's pocket." The subject (someone) is doing the action (picking), and the object (Suman's pocket) is receiving the action.

Therefore,the correct answer is option no.(4) Additional Information

  • Option 1, "Someone has being picked Suman's pocket," is incorrect because "being" is not needed in passive voice constructions. It also uses the wrong form of the verb "pick." -
  • Option 2, "Suman's pocket had picked," is incorrect because it uses the wrong form of the verb "pick" and the wrong tense. "Had picked" is past perfect, which is used to indicate an action that was completed before another past action. -
  • Option 3, "Suman's pocket been picked," is incorrect because it is missing the auxiliary verb "has been" and the main verb "picked" is in the wrong form.

Key Points

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the active voice and it is in the present continuous tense.
  • When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'The invigilator' of the active voice becomes the object, the object 'the students' becomes the subject.
  • The active format "is + V1 (advise) + ing" should be converted into the passive format "are + being + V3 (advised)".
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the present continuous tense.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Additional Information

  • Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:
     
    TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION
    Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him
    Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him
    Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him
    Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual
    Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him
    Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him
    Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him
    Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him
    Future Continuous He will be playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him
    Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual

 

Hinglish

  • Active Voice में , एक वाक्य विषय पर जोर देता है, एक क्रिया करता है।
  • Passive Voice में , एक वाक्य वाक्य की क्रिया या वस्तु पर जोर देता है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य active voice में है और यह present continuous tense में है।
  • जब हम इस वाक्य को passive voice में बदलते हैं, तो active voice का subject 'The invigilator', object बन जाता है और object 'the students', subject बन जाता है।
  • Active format "is + V1 (advise) + ing" को passive format "are + being + V3 (advised)" में परिवर्तित किया जाना चाहिए।
  • यह present continuous tense के लिए active and passive voice rule है।
